omniroute.name: OmniRoute
omniroute.what: A local gateway that routes your IDE or CLI to many providers through one OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

needs.label: Node.js 22.22.2 or newer (below 23, or 24 up to 26)

install.why: installs the omniroute command globally

after: Open http://localhost:20128, connect a provider with your own account or API key, then point your tool at http://localhost:20128/v1 with an OmniRoute API key.
Optional: `omniroute autostart enable` starts it at login.

freellmapi.name: FreeLLMAPI
freellmapi.what: One OpenAI-compatible /v1 endpoint that stacks the free tiers of many LLM providers and fails over between them.

install.why: sets up ~/freellmapi, makes an encryption key, pulls the image and starts the container. Safe to re-run; it keeps your .env

install.manual: Use the desktop installer on the project's GitHub Releases page: https://github.com/tashfeenahmed/freellmapi/releases

update.why: re-running updates the container and keeps your .env

after: If it is installed but not running, re-run the install step: it keeps your .env and starts the container. Open http://localhost:3001, add provider keys on the Keys page, then use the unified key with base URL http://localhost:3001/v1.

strix.name: Strix
strix.what: Autonomous AI penetration testing that proves vulnerabilities with working exploits.

install.why: installs the strix command in its own environment
the project's own installer, used when pipx is missing

after: Set a model and key before a scan, for example: export STRIX_LLM="openai/gpt-5.4" and export LLM_API_KEY=... . The managed cloud (`strix cloud ...`) needs neither Docker nor a local key.

agent-reach.name: Agent Reach
agent-reach.what: Gives an agent access to internet platforms (social sites, video, search) through one set of tools.

install.why: installs the agent-reach command in its own environment

after: Run `agent-reach install --env=auto` for a read-only check of what is missing, and `agent-reach doctor` to see which channels work. Add `--system` only if you agree to let it install system packages.

claude-mem.name: claude-mem
claude-mem.what: Persistent memory across agent sessions: hooks, a background worker, search and timelines.

install.why: registers the hooks and starts the worker; it may ask you to sign in. Pass --provider, or set CLAUDE_MEM_ONLINE_OPTIN=false, to skip sign-in. For another IDE add --ide <name>. Do not use `npm install -g claude-mem`: that installs only the library

after: Restart the agent so the hooks load.

ecc.name: ECC (Everything Claude Code) add-on
ecc.what: ECC's agents, hooks, commands and rules, which a skills folder cannot carry. SFP already includes ECC's skills.

install.why: ECC's guided setup. Use one ECC install method per IDE; stacking methods duplicates skills and hooks

after: Start a new session and run `/plugin list` to confirm ecc@ecc is enabled. See docs/INTEGRATION.md for the other IDEs.

agentshield.name: ECC AgentShield
agentshield.what: A scanner for agent configuration and skills.

install.why: installs the ecc-agentshield command globally

graphify.name: Graphify
graphify.what: Maps a project (code, docs, PDFs, images) into a knowledge graph you can query instead of grepping files.

install.why: installs the graphify command in its own environment (the package is named graphifyy, with two y)
the alternative when uv is missing

after: Run `graphify install` once: it detects your assistant and registers the skill and hooks. If `graphify` is not found afterwards, run `uv tool update-shell` and restart the shell. Then type `/graphify .` in the project. Needs uv or pipx; with neither, install one first.

difftastic.name: Difftastic
difftastic.what: A structural diff tool that compares code syntax rather than lines.

install.why: compiles and installs the difft binary via Cargo

after: Run `difft <file1> <file2>` to compare code ASTs.

browser-use.name: Browser-Use
browser-use.what: Make websites accessible for AI agents via Playwright and Chromium.

install.why: installs the browser-use Python library

after: Install browser binaries with `playwright install chromium`.

opencode.name: OpenCode
opencode.what: Open-source AI coding agent CLI and desktop interface.

install.why: installs the opencode command globally via npm

after: Run `opencode` inside any project directory to launch the assistant.

skillspector.name: SkillSpector
skillspector.what: Security scanner for AI agent skills from NVIDIA.

install.why: installs skillspector CLI

after: Run `skillspector scan <folder> --no-llm` to scan an agent skill directory.

openviking.name: OpenViking
openviking.what: A context database and virtual filesystem for AI agents.

install.why: installs openviking CLI

after: Run `viking init` to initialize the agent context filesystem.

searxng.name: SearXNG
searxng.what: Privacy-respecting, hackable metasearch engine aggregating results from over 70 search services.

install.why: pulls the official SearXNG container image

after: Start with `docker run -d -p 8080:8080 -v ./searxng:/etc/searxng searxng/searxng`.

agentmemory.name: AgentMemory
agentmemory.what: Persistent vector memory MCP server and store for AI coding agents.

install.why: installs the AgentMemory MCP server globally

after: Add to your IDE MCP configuration using `npx -y @agentmemory/agentmemory`.

gitnexus.name: GitNexus
gitnexus.what: Knowledge graph and AST code indexing tool for multi-repository context.

install.why: installs the GitNexus CLI globally

after: Run `npx gitnexus analyze` in any git repository to build the graph.

openmontage.name: OpenMontage
openmontage.what: Programmatic video montage creation pipeline using FFmpeg and Remotion.

install.why: installs the OpenMontage CLI globally

after: Run `openmontage --help` to inspect montage synthesis options.

graft.name: Graft
graft.what: Multi-agent pipeline compiler and runtime CLI for composing agent workflows.

install.why: installs the Graft agent compiler globally

after: Run `graft init` to scaffold a multi-agent pipeline definition.

trail-code.name: Trail-Code
trail-code.what: AST dependency mapper and codebase learnings layer for AI agents.

install.why: installs the Trail-Code agent layer globally

after: Run `npx trail-code watch` in your repository root.

colibri.name: Colibri
colibri.what: Ultra-lightweight pure C Mixture-of-Experts streaming inference engine.

install.why: clones Colibri repository for local compilation with make

after: Compile with `make` and run `./colibri --model <path>`.
